error_signature: DataXceiver error processing WRITE_BLOCK operation java.io.IOException Broken pipe
symptom: Data node write failures during block replication, client retries repeatedly then job stalls
root_cause: Network instability or datanode disk saturation causing write pipeline to break mid-transfer
resolution: Checked datanode disk I/O with iostat, found disk near capacity; added datanode to exclude list, triggered re-replication, freed disk space

error_signature: Slow BlockReceiver write packet to mirror took longer than expected
symptom: Intermittent slow writes reported by multiple clients, no job failure yet but latency climbing
root_cause: Datanode under memory pressure causing GC pauses that stall the write pipeline
resolution: Reviewed GC logs, increased datanode heap size, tuned young-gen ratio, restarted datanode during low-traffic window

error_signature: NameNode not yet started java.io.IOException Call From to failed on connection exception
symptom: All jobs fail immediately at startup with connection refused to NameNode
root_cause: NameNode process crashed or is still in safe mode after restart, replaying edit logs
resolution: Checked NameNode logs, confirmed it was replaying a large edit log after an ungraceful shutdown; waited for safe mode exit, then investigated why shutdown was ungraceful (OOM kill)

symptom: Spark job stages retry repeatedly, some executors marked as lost, job eventually fails or runs very slow
root_cause: Executor JVM under heavy GC pressure due to skewed partition causing OOM-adjacent memory pressure, heartbeat thread starved
resolution: Identified data skew via Spark UI stage metrics, repartitioned on a higher-cardinality key, increased executor memory as stopgap

symptom: Shuffle stage fails partway through, downstream stages blocked, job retries from checkpoint
root_cause: An executor was killed (likely by YARN/K8s due to exceeding memory limits) while other executors were still fetching shuffle blocks from it
resolution: Checked resource manager logs for OOM-kill events, increased executor memory overhead setting, reduced shuffle partition size to lower per-task memory footprint

error_signature: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError Java heap space during collect operation
symptom: Driver crashes when action is called, job fails immediately with heap dump written
root_cause: A .collect() call pulled a dataset far larger than the driver's configured heap size back to the driver node
resolution: Replaced collect() with a write-to-storage pattern, or used take()/sample() for debugging; increased driver memory as a short-term fix

error_signature: Task exited with return code 1 UPSTREAM_FAILED
symptom: Downstream tasks in DAG marked upstream_failed, pipeline run shows red across multiple tasks
root_cause: A single upstream extraction task failed due to a source API timeout, cascading failure through the DAG
resolution: Checked source API status page, confirmed transient outage; added retry with exponential backoff and circuit breaker to the extraction task

error_signature: sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError could not connect to server Connection timed out
symptom: Scheduler and multiple tasks fail simultaneously trying to write task state to metadata DB
root_cause: Metadata database connection pool exhausted due to a spike in concurrently scheduled tasks exceeding max_connections
resolution: Increased DB max_connections and Airflow pool size, added SQL connection pooling (pgbouncer) in front of metadata DB

error_signature: FATAL too many connections for role
symptom: New pipeline jobs fail to connect to warehouse DB, existing connections still function
root_cause: A long-running ETL job left connections open without closing them (connection leak), exhausting the role's connection quota
resolution: Audited ETL scripts for missing connection.close() in finally blocks, added context managers, set statement_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout

error_signature: deadlock detected Process waiting for ShareLock on transaction
symptom: Concurrent load jobs into the same table intermittently fail with deadlock errors
root_cause: Two ETL jobs updating overlapping row ranges in different order, causing lock-order inversion
resolution: Changed load strategy to stage-then-swap (load into temp table, then atomic rename) instead of in-place upserts, eliminating row-level lock contention

error_signature: org.apache.kafka.common.errors.TimeoutException Expiring records due to metadata not available
symptom: Producers intermittently fail to publish events, consumer lag begins climbing
root_cause: A broker was under-replicated after a rolling restart, causing partition leader elections and metadata propagation delay
resolution: Checked broker logs for under-replicated partitions, waited for ISR to catch up, tuned replica.lag.time.max.ms and reduced restart batch size for future rollouts

error_signature: Consumer group rebalance failed Member ID required
symptom: Consumers stuck in a repeated rebalance loop, no messages being processed, lag grows unbounded
root_cause: A consumer instance had a session.timeout.ms too low relative to processing time, causing it to be dropped and rejoin repeatedly
resolution: Increased session.timeout.ms and max.poll.interval.ms, moved heavy per-record processing off the poll thread into an async worker pool

error_signature: Schema mismatch column count expected 12 got 11 during load
symptom: Daily load job fails validation step immediately after extract, no rows loaded
root_cause: Upstream source system silently dropped a column in a schema change without notifying downstream consumers
resolution: Added schema drift detection step before load using a schema registry contract check, alerted upstream team, added a nullable-column fallback for non-breaking changes

error_signature: Duplicate key value violates unique constraint during merge
symptom: Incremental load job fails on merge/upsert step with primary key violation
root_cause: A late-arriving duplicate record from a replayed message queue was not deduplicated before merge
resolution: Added idempotency key based dedup step before merge, using a rolling dedup window keyed on event_id

error_signature: Task killed due to zombie or exceeded execution_timeout
symptom: A single task in the DAG runs far longer than usual then is force-killed, no clear error in task logs
root_cause: Source table had grown significantly and a full-table scan query (missing partition filter) started taking hours instead of minutes
resolution: Added partition pruning filter to the query, added query duration monitoring with alerting threshold at 2x historical p95
